interest: Shows Consul Boyce debunking press claims of mass Nisei repatriation to Japan in 1937-38, backed by travel statistics.
overview: This file (894.5511) contains U.S. State Department correspondence and cross-references from December 1936 to March 1939 concerning immigration and travel between the United States and Japan. The file begins with a 1936 cross-reference sheet regarding Japanese passport requirements for naval personnel and passengers traveling to Guam via Yokohama on the USS Gold Star. The core of the file consists of a February 1939 despatch from American Consul Richard F. Boyce in Yokohama examining travel patterns of second-generation Japanese Americans (Nisei) following the outbreak of the Second Sino-Japanese War ('China Incident') in July 1937. Addressing press reports that anti-Japanese sentiment in the U.S. or militaristic enthusiasm was driving young Japanese Americans to repatriate, Boyce presents port data showing an actual 30 percent drop in travel to Japan between 1937 and 1938. The file concludes with Far Eastern Affairs division clearance and a formal request from the Secretary of State to the Secretary of Labor to obtain updated entry and departure figures from the Bureau of Immigration for Pacific Coast ports and Honolulu.

subfiles.about: Cross-reference note concerning Japanese passport regulations for passengers on the naval supply ship USS Gold Star traveling to Guam.
subfiles.summary: Boyce reports Japan will no longer accept USS Gold Star passengers' Guam identity certificates without consular guarantee, and recommends issuing standard passports to Guam personnel.

subfiles.about: Consular despatch reporting on the travel patterns of second-generation Japanese Americans and requesting updated entry and departure statistics.
subfiles.summary: Boyce reports a 30% drop in 1937-38 departures to Japan, refuting press claims of rising Nisei repatriation over prejudice or military enlistment, and asks for updated Pacific port and Honolulu travel statistics.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 475 from Consul Richard F. Boyce on repatriation and travel of Americans of Japanese race

subfiles.about: Departmental memorandum approving the consular request for Japanese American migration and travel statistics.
subfiles.summary: Ballantine approves Boyce's request for Immigration Bureau statistics on Japanese American entries and departures through Pacific ports and Honolulu.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Division of Far Eastern Affairs on travel statistics for Japanese Americans

subfiles.about: Official diplomatic communication requesting the Department of Labor to supply immigration statistics on Japanese American travelers.
subfiles.summary: State asks the Labor Department for entry and departure statistics on Japanese American citizens at Pacific Coast ports and Honolulu since July 1938.
subfiles.title: Letter from Secretary of State to Secretary of Labor requesting immigration statistics
